title: Spring Framework 7.0: @CacheEvict on a method returning Flux emits only the first element
errorSample:

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue/PR; short error excerpt quoted.

symptom: A service method annotated with @CacheEvict that returns a Flux processes and saves every item, but the caller receives only the first element and then onComplete. A StepVerifier fails with expected onNext(two) but actual onComplete().
cause: The cache interceptor's reactive handling for @CacheEvict-advised methods that return a Flux truncates the returned publisher to its first element. This is a Spring Framework bug fixed in 7.0.10.
fixSummary: Remove @CacheEvict from the method and clear the cache inside the reactive pipeline instead: inject CacheManager and call cacheManager.getCache("items")?.clear() from doOnComplete on the returned Flux, which keeps the full Flux and the eviction. Changing the return type to Mono<List<T>> also avoids it but changes the callers' contract. Upgrading to Framework 7.0.10 fixes it at the source.
